backstory:
Adoub Bin Hessar was born in the saddle, or near enough that the difference never mattered to the Darabin. Among the Horse Lords a man is his mount, his lance, and his share of the last raid, and Adoub has owned all three since he was old enough to hold them. He is a raider by trade and makes no apology for it; in the deep desert the strong drink and the weak walk, and the Darabin have always chosen to ride.

His mother's people were Banirga stock, which is why he carries the Bin before his father's name, and his father was a captive broken to the herd who won his place back with a spear. From them Adoub learned the two desert virtues that count: water is never wasted, and strength is never hidden. He has bled Ja'arut caravans and Hamisab patrols alike, and pays the Sultan's tax only when the Sultan's riders are close enough to collect it.

He respects two things, a stronger arm and a fuller waterskin, and has no use for settled folk who mistake walls for safety. The desert will outlast their walls, he says, and so will he.

Personality: proud, blunt, fiercely loyal to his riders.
Mannerisms: measures every stranger by their hands and their horse.
Appearance: sun-cracked skin, a tribal brand at the throat, a curved blade slung across the back.
Flaws: cannot let a challenge to his strength go unanswered.
